title: True or False (1 point each, 10 total)
instructions: Select True or False for each statement. Read CAREFULLY.

questions.question: In C#, every statement must end with a semicolon.
C# is case-sensitive, so the names score and Score are treated as two different variables.
A do-while loop always runs its body at least once.
The break keyword only skips the rest of the current loop iteration and then keeps looping.
Comments in your code are ignored by the computer when the program runs.
If you pass an int variable into a method and change the parameter inside that method, the original variable outside the method stays the same.
Two methods can share the same name as long as their parameter lists are different.
A variable declared inside one method can be used freely inside a different method of the same class.
RAM keeps all of its contents even after the computer is powered off.
One method is allowed to call another method.
